articles.title: World Matchplay Darts: Luke Littler blows Josh Rock away and Dirk van Duijvenbode wins thriller against Gary Anderson to set up semi-final showdown
articles.summary: Luke Littler averaged 109.57 in a comprehensive display against Josh Rock; he will take on Dirk van Duijvenbode who won a thrilling match against Gary Anderson; you can watch the World Matchplay live on Sky Sports in Blackpool until July 26
articles.body:
Litter beat Rock 16-7 as he looks to become the first person to go back-to-back at this tournament since Michael van Gerwen a decade ago.

In what is turning into a tournament for the record books, Littler's stats impressed once again. He posted a 109.57 average with 17 180s and a 53 per cent success rate on the doubles.

"Another brilliant game for myself. I've gone 109, 113, 109 again [averages] so I've just got to keep it going," Littler told Sky Sports .

"Fair play to Josh. He gave me a really good game there. I think it was the third session where I won all five legs.

"I kind of got myself into that lead and I just had to stay there and got the job done."

Littler and Rock met at the semi-final stage of this tournament just one year ago when Littler won an 18-15 epic, hitting a nine-darter on way.

However after a close opening 10 legs to get Thursday's match going, it was all Littler as he romped into another semi-final.

Rock was in the zone early in the contest and matched every break of throw that was thrown at him, a 129 checkout from 'The Nuke' a highlight as the pair of young stars looked in a real battle at 5-5.

However, as is now customary from Littler, he took control in second session to reel off five legs in a row. Remarkably, Rock did not get a dart at double in that period.

He increased that dominance to seven legs in a row before Rock could stop the onslaught. Two holds of throw were all that the Northern Irishman managed as he sat 13-6 behind.

The final blow then came in the 23rd leg when the 19-year-old broke Rock's throw again as he cleaned up 44.

With that, the defending champion came to hold his throw and with his third match dart, took his favourite D10.

Van Duijvenbode holds on after Anderson rally

Van Duijvenbode held off a phenomenal fightback from Anderson in a 16-13 thriller to book a spot in the semi-finals in Blackpool for the first time in his career.

The Dutchman was 15-8 ahead, just one from victory, when Anderson roared back and averaged over 114 to take five legs in a row including a massive 154 checkout. It looked like he simply was going to pull off a miracle.

However, just when he needed it, Van Duijvenbode found his form to pin D10 for a massive win.

"To be fair the break couldn't come at a worse moment. You just know Gary loves the game. He never gives up," Van Duijvenbode told Sky Sports .

"He's probably the best in the world when he hits the trebles.

"I expected [the 154]. He didn't miss, but I always think my opponent will hit it."

The Dutchman added: "At some point I felt nerves in my stomach."

The opening session went the way of Van Duijvenbode, with the Dutchman finding two breaks of throw and finishing off the five legs with a 107 checkout to romp into a 4-1 lead.

The second session was similar to the first and when Van Duijvenbode found another break of throw and followed it with a clutch 112 checkout, it was looking ominous for Anderson with his opponent 8-3 ahead.

Anderson had work to do and he got going by taking out three legs on the spin, including a clutch bullseye finish for 84, to get back into the contest.

Van Duijvenbode stopped the rot with a hold of throw but had been reeled back into a contest at 9-6.

That was until Van Duijvenbode came back out on fire while the Flying Scotsman fell away in the next session with the Dutchman taking all five legs.

Anderson's throw was broken three times with a miracle looking the only option for the former world champion as he sat 14-6 behind.

And so nearly did a miracle occur. Anderson showed just he is one of the greats of the game, but Van Duijvenbode found the singular moment he needed to finally get over the line.

What is happening on Friday at the World Matchplay Darts?

The quarter-finals continue on Friday at the World Matchplay, live from 7.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event and Action.

Gian van Veen and James Wade will do battle in the quarter-finals for a second year in a row, with the world No 3 looking to avenge his loss to 'The Machine' in 2025.

Then, Gerwyn Price faces Ross Smith. Smith is through to the quarter-finals after Cameron Menzies withdrew from their second round match in the fourth leg due to illness.

Who will win this year's World Matchplay Darts? Luke Littler will be defending his title and you can watch all the action on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more top sport with NOW .

articles.title: Betfred World Matchplay 2026 schedule and results: Round-by-round scores from Blackpool as Luke Littler defended his title
articles.summary: Round-by-round results from the Betfred World Matchplay, where defending champion Luke Littler beat former world No 1 Gerwyn Price 18-9 to successfully defend his title at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool; Price finished runner-up for a second time in four years
articles.body:
Defending champion Luke Littler became the first player since Michael van Gerwen to retain the title in Blackpool, producing a tournament-record average as he sealed an emphatic 18-9 victory over Gerwyn Price.

Littler previously came past Niko Springer in his tournament opener ahead of beating Nathan Aspinall in a second-round thriller, before thrashing Josh Rock and Dirk van Duijvenbode to breeze through to the final.

2022 runner-up Price edged past Martin Schindler in his tournament opener and then improved to beat Rob Cross in the next round, before defeating Ross Smith to continue his record of reaching every TV major semi-final this season.

Price saw off Gian van Veen 16-13 to reach his first major TV final since 2023, with the victory lifting him to world No 4 and seeing him leapfrog Jonny Clayton as the highest-ranked Welshman.

The event featured the top 16 players from the PDC Werner Rankings Ladder as well as the best 16 players from the one-year ProTour rankings.

Prize purses for the 2026 event have been boosted to £1m, with the winner set to pocket £225,000. Littler reaching the final guarantees him becoming the first player in history to break £3m in prize money.

articles.title: Eve Muirhead: Olympic champion makes curling return with Bobby Lammie in Scottish Mixed Doubles
articles.summary: Olympic champion Eve Muirhead makes her comeback at the Scottish Mixed Curling Championships on Thursday after revoking her retirement.
articles.body:
When you've won Olympic gold, you don't enter subsequent events with anything other than winning them in your mind. Eve Muirhead knows that. But she also knows that this is her first curling competition in four years.

The 36-year-old makes her return on Thursday after revoking her retirement when she plays in the Scottish Mixed Doubles Championship in Aberdeen.

Muirhead will reprise her 2022 world title winning partnership with Bobby Lammie - himself a twice Olympic silver medallist - in what the duo hope will be the beginning of a four-year campaign that culminates in the Alpes 2030 Games.

They come into this domestic competition as the big-ticket pairing - having never lost a competitive game - but also as target for the rest of a stacked field.

"We can't put too much pressure on ourselves," Muirhead told BBC Sport Scotland. "I need to remember I've been away for over four years now and I'm just back into it.

"I know our competitive side is going to come out but we need to put things in perspective as well. We've got to remember that it's a long project that we're in."

Selected matches from Aberdeen streamed live

Muirhead says she has been gripped by a combination of excitement and nerves as she prepares for her comeback.

Six round-robin games across Thursday, Friday and Saturday - and potentially a play-off later that day - will decide if she and Lammie reach Sunday's semis and final, with a selection of their matches live on the BBC.

While the duo know each other's games well, the fact Lammie is Stirling-based and Muirhead trains in Preston has limited their ice time. However, they meet up every couple of weeks and believe they are in a good place for their return.

"We've got pressure on us and eyes on us as a combination but I think we've got to forget about that and just go out and be us," Muirhead said. "That's what we did when we when we won the Scottish Champs in 2022 and went on to win the worlds.

"But the standard of teams in Aberdeen is very, very high - probably one of the strongest ever in a Scottish champs - so it's going to be tough. We just need to curl how we know we can and make sure and do the small parts right and the rest will take take care of itself."

articles.title: Archers, shooters fire India’s medal rush on a golden day at Asian Games
articles.summary: India had its best day of the Asian Games so far as compound archers won all three team gold medals, while shooters Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai also
articles.body: India had its best day of the Asian Games so far as compound archers won all three team gold medals, while shooters Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai also finished on top in the mixed trap event.Three bronze medals in boxing and wrestling took India’s overall tally to 60 medals - 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze. India also moved up to eighth place from 10th on Tuesday.Compound archers complete gold sweepThe compound archers were the stars of the day, successfully defending all three team titles.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha and Prithika Pradeep started the gold rush by winning the women’s team event. They beat China’s Wunier, Yue Wang and Fangyao Wei 238-234. The Indian score equalled the world record.Chikitha and Sahil Jadhav then won the mixed team gold. They held their nerve against Korea’s Jungyoon Park and Choi Eun Gyu to win 158-157 after a shoot-off.The victory also helped India secure an Olympic quota place. India became the first country to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics mixed team compound event, which will make its Olympic debut in Los Angeles.The men’s team of Kushal Dalal, Sahil and Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru completed the clean sweep. They beat China’s Jiahao Liao, Jinyi Liu and Jingyu Shi 238-237 in the final.Chikitha and Sahil finished the day with two gold medals each.Neeru, Kynan overcome early setbackAt the shooting range, Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai recovered from a difficult start to win the mixed trap gold.The Indian pair finished with a score of 34, setting an Asian and Games record.It was Neeru’s second gold of the Games. She had earlier won the individual trap gold and also played a key role in India’s silver medal-winning women’s trap team.With two golds and a silver, Neeru became the most successful Indian athlete at the ongoing Games.India women reach hockey finalThe Indian women’s hockey team also had a strong day, beating Korea 2-0 in the semifinal to reach the final.The victory assured India of at least a silver medal and improved on the bronze they won at the previous Asian Games.Boxers shineIndia’s boxers have already bettered their medal tally from the previous edition. They won four medals in Hangzhou, while six medals are assured this time.Lovlina Borgohain reached the women’s 75kg final after edging Kazakhstan’s Natalya Bogdanova, the reigning 70kg world champion, 3-2.However, Asian Games debutant Priya Ghanghas lost 1-4 to former world champion Yang Chengyu of China in the 60kg semifinal.Another debutant, Kapil, also lost 1-4 to Uzbekistan’s reigning world champion Turabek Khabibullaev in the 90kg semifinal.India will have three boxers fighting for gold on Friday — Lovlina, Parveen Hooda (65kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg).Priya, Kapil and super-heavyweight boxer Narender Berwal will return home with bronze medals.Sunil gives India wrestling bronzeSunil Kumar became the first Indian Greco-Roman wrestler to win two Asian Games medals after securing bronze in the men’s 87kg category.Sunil defeated the Philippines’ Roberts Callum Johnston 9-0 by technical superiority to secure a place on the podium.He had also won bronze at the Hangzhou Games, ending India’s 13-year wait for a Greco-Roman wrestling medal.Nisha Dahiya, however, finished without a medal in the women’s 68kg category.India secure medals in squashBoth Indian squash teams booked their places in the semifinals and assured themselves of medals.The men’s team, the top seeds and defending champions, beat Kuwait 2-0 in the quarterfinals.Veer Chotrani defeated articles.title: Dylan Larkin stayed close to his Michigan roots: The family story behind the Detroit Red Wings captain and his journey from local hockey to NHL stardom
articles.summary: Explore Dylan Larkin's remarkable journey from a young Red Wings fan in Michigan to the captain of the Detroit Red Wings. Discover his family's sporting legacy and how his Michigan roots shaped his hockey career.
articles.body: Dylan Larkin’s Detroit Red Wings roots run deep before he ever laced ’em up in the NHL. Growing up in Waterford, he was a Red Wings fan who regularly attended games as a child. He played in local programs before moving up to the U.S. National Team Development Program and college hockey at the University of Michigan.That path eventually led Larkin to Detroit, which selected him 15th overall in the 2014 NHL Draft. What started as a childhood relationship with the franchise turned into a professional career, with Larkin eventually captaining the team he watched growing up.Dylan Larkin’s Michigan roots shaped Detroit Red Wings journeyLarkin's parents, Kevin and Denise, raised him in Waterford and encouraged him and his older brother Colin to play sports. The family also frequently attended Detroit Red Wings games, giving him an early connection to the NHL organization that would be his professional home.He also did most of his development as a youth hockey player in the area. Larkin played for programs including the Lakeland Hawks, Honeybaked and Belle Tire before moving to a higher-level development environment.One of the more memorable connections to the Red Wings came during the team's Stanley Cup championship celebration in 2002. Larkin was just a kid when he attended the parade down Woodward Avenue, part of his early connection with the franchise.Dylan Larkin’s Michigan roots and hockey journeyLarkin continued his development in the U.S. National Team Development Program in Ann Arbor. The program was a huge step toward elite hockey before he went to the University of Michigan.Larkin, one of the bright young stars in college hockey in his freshman year with the Wolverines, was selected as the Big Ten Freshman of the Year.Detroit’s 2014 selection of him came full circle for his journey. Larkin went from a kid watching the Red Wings to wearing the franchise’s jersey in the NHL. His progress in the organization eventually led to the captaincy.Dylan Larkin’s family built a lasting sports legacyThe Larkin family’s sporting background began with soccer, not hockey. Kevin Larkin grew up in Scarborough, Ontario after his family emigrated from Dublin, Ireland. Kevin, his brother Paul and his brother Jimmy were all good soccer players and played at U.S. colleges.Kevin attended the University of Southern Indiana, where he met Denise. His brother Jimmy became a professional goalkeeper and played internationally for Canada.Dylan and Colin were shaped by that sporting environment from an early age. Both brothers played soccer and hockey, but the family decided to focus on hockey because of the demands and costs of playing two sports.Later, Colin played NCAA Division III hockey at UMass Boston before turning pro with opportunities in the American Hockey League and ECHL.Dylan Larkin’s family life beyond Detroit Red WingsLarkin’s story has changed off the ice, too. He married Kenzy Wolfe in August 2023 at Shepherd’s Hollow Golf Club in Clarkston, Michigan, near the community where he was raised.The couple later lost a child before welcoming their daughter, Lennyn Marie Larkin, in May 2025.So his personal journey has stayed tightly linked to the place his hockey career started. articles.title: Ahora sí, todos se rinden a Lamine
articles.standfirst: El español se convierte en el nuevo favorito para hacerse con el Balón de Oro tras su exhibición ante Croacia
articles.summary: El español se convierte en el nuevo favorito para hacerse con el Balón de Oro tras su exhibición ante Croacia
articles.body: Durante buena parte de este año, Harry Kane ha sido el inquilino indiscutible de la cima en las quinielas del Balón de Oro. Sus números de la temporada pasada, 61 goles en 51 partidos con el Bayern de Múnich y 73 en total sumando su etapa con Inglaterra, lo situaron en registros que no se veían desde la época dorada de Messi y Cristiano Ronaldo. El propio delantero no dudó en defender su candidatura en MARCA: "los 73 goles hablan por sí solos". Sin embargo, las últimas semanas han supuesto un vuelco copernicano en el mercado de apuestas del Balón de Oro, con Lamine Yamal desbancando al inglés como principal favorito. Es cierto que, supuestamente, sólo se debe tener en cuenta la temporada 25-26, en este caso hasta que concluyó el Mundial, para determinar quién merece el Balón de Oro. También que las votaciones están cerradas desde ayer. No obstante, la mayoría de casas de apuestas seguían manteniendo ayer a Harry Kane como favorito, eso sí, ya con Lamine respirándole en la nuca, cuando hace apenas dos semanas el inglés era el claro candidato a ganar el este trofeo del que pocos pueden presumir. Pero el vuelco total a las quinielas no ha llegado, curiosamente, hasta justo después de la goleada de España por 4-1 a Croacia en la Nations League, que tuvo lugar en la noche del martes, con una exhibición de Lamine Yamal. Abrió el marcador a los dos minutos con un violento remate de zurda tras una jugada de 25 pases, asistió a Marc Pubill para el segundo tanto español en el minuto 31, y selló su particular noche mágica con un nuevo gol en el 63, definiendo con clase desde un ángulo complicado tras un pase de Pedri. Opta destacó además un dato histórico: España ha marcado en los dos primeros minutos de juego en partidos consecutivos, ante Inglaterra y ante Croacia, ambos con la firma de Yamal. El resultado deja a la 'Roja' líder de su grupo con pleno de puntos, encadenando su segunda goleada tras la ajustada victoria en Wembley ante los ingleses, precisamente el equipo de su gran rival en esta carrera. El mercado de apuestas ya ha asimilado por completo este giro. Lamine Yamal se paga desde 1.67 en Bet365 o Codere hasta 1.90 en Tonybet, cifras que lo sitúan como principal favorito en la práctica totalidad de operadores consultados. Harry Kane, por su parte, oscila entre el 1.9 de Tonybet y el 2.15 de Codere, todavía competitivo pero ya relegado a segunda opción en la mayoría de casas. Por detrás de este duelo de dos aparece Kylian Mbappé, cuya cuota se mueve entre 11 y 15 según el operador, una distancia que confirma que, pese a su temporada goleadora, el francés no termina de entrar en la conversación principal. Leo Messi se mantiene estable en 15 en la gran mayoría de casas, un reconocimiento a su legado más que a su rendimiento actual. Y Rodri es quien presenta el rango más amplio de todos los candidatos, desde 15 hasta 34 según el operador, reflejo de las dudas que persisten sobre su continuidad tras las lesiones que lastraron su temporada. Lo de Yamal no es flor de un día. El extremo del Barcelona llega a esta ventana de octubre en el mejor momento de su carrera: campeón del mundo este verano tras la final ante Argentina, campeón de LaLiga con el Barcelona, y ahora también protagonista destacado del arranque liguero azulgrana, donde ha sido determinante en la reconversión ofensiva del equipo de Hansi Flick. A sus 19 años recién cumplidos, acumula ya un palmarés que incluye la Eurocopa de 2024, dos ligas españolas, una Copa del Rey y dos Supercopas, un currículum que pocos futbolistas pueden exhibir a su edad y que refuerza su candidatura frente a rivales con más trayectoria pero, quizás, menos impacto colectivo esta temporada. El contraste con Kane resulta especialmente llamativo. Tras su histórica campaña 2025/26, el delantero del Bayern ha comenzado la nueva temporada con un ritmo goleador mucho más contenido, lejos todavía de las cifras que lo convirtieron en el gran dominador del mercado hace apenas unos meses. Esa desaceleración, sumada al impacto mediático y deportivo de Yamal, explica el vuelco que ahora reflejan las casas de apuestas.

articles.title: Desde Portugal presionan a Néstor Lorenzo: la condición con Luis Suárez para los amistosos
articles.standfirst: La firme exigencia que llega desde Sporting de Portugal a Néstor Lorenzo por Luis Suárez
articles.summary: La firme exigencia que llega desde Sporting de Portugal a Néstor Lorenzo por Luis Suárez
articles.body: La Selección Colombia de Néstor Lorenzo afronta una nueva ventana de partidos amistosos internacionales en territorio norteamericano. Sin embargo, la atención periodística y deportiva no solo se centra en el rendimiento táctico de la 'Tricolor', sino también en las presiones e inquietudes que llegan desde Europa por parte de los clubes dueños de los derechos deportivos de sus principales figuras. Un reporte publicado por el diario portugués A Bola, reveló la solicitud enviada desde Lisboa a la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol respecto al manejo físico del delantero samario Luis Javier Suárez, pieza clave en el esquema ofensivo del Sporting CP. El club portugués se puso en contacto con el cuerpo técnico encabezado por Néstor Lorenzo para transmitirle un pedido especial: dosificar las cargas y administrar los minutos en cancha de Luis Javier Suárez durante los encuentros de la fecha FIFA. El motivo principal obedece al exigente calendario que le espera al delantero en el ámbito de clubes. Suárez viene desempeñando un rol protagónico tanto en la Primeira Liga como en la UEFA Champions League, torneos donde el Sporting disputa puntos decisivos y busca mantener vivas sus aspiraciones en la temporada. Ante la alta exigencia competitiva en Europa, la dirigencia y el departamento médico de las 'Águilas' buscan evitar un desgaste excesivo o eventuales lesiones musculares. El primer compromiso de esta serie de amistosos ofreció pistas sobre cómo el cuerpo técnico colombiano está manejando la situación. En el partido disputado en el M&T Bank Stadium de Baltimore frente a la Selección de México, Luis Javier Suárez arrancó como titular y anotó el gol de la 'Tricolor' al minuto 9 de juego. Atendiendo a la gestión de tiempos y al plan trazado: Para el seleccionador Néstor Lorenzo, el panorama requiere un equilibrio entre las pretensiones de los clubes europeos y la necesidad de afianzar la idea táctica del equipo nacional. Suárez ha consolidado un crecimiento sostenido, demostrando efectividad tanto en Eliminatorias, torneo continental y en compromisos de preparación internacional. Aunque los partidos no otorgan puntos oficiales, para la Selección Colombia representan oportunidades valiosas de ajustar el circuito ofensivo y ensayar alternativas tácticas. Lorenzo deberá equilibrar los minutos de Suárez con la participación de otros atacantes en la convocatoria, respetando la recomendación venida desde Portugal sin descuidar el rodaje futbolístico de la Selección.

articles.title: Jared Bednar, Avalanche Agree to New Contract Ahead of 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche are recommitting to their longtime head coach after last season's Presidents' Trophy win and Western Conference Finals loss.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche are recommitting to their longtime head coach after last season's Presidents' Trophy win and Western Conference Finals loss.

The Avalanche have signed Jared Bednar to a four-year contract extension, the team announced Wednesday.

Rangers Will Be Better, But Not a Contender

The Avalanche are preparing to open the 2026-27 season Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Kings.

The new contract is set to keep Bednar in Colorado through the 2030-31 season.

Bednar is heading into his 11th season with the Avalanche, which he led to a Stanley Cup in 2022.

The news comes after president of hockey operations Joe Sakic added general manager to his job title following Chris MacFarland's departure for the Nashville Predators.

Bednar said in a Wednesday appearance on Altitude Sports Radio 92.5 he had engaged in contract talks with Sakic throughout the offseason.

"Joe and I have had multiple conversations over the summer... I don't think either one of us was like, 'We have to have it done by this date,' but it's nice to get it put to bed and just be able to focus on what we have to do this season," Bednar said.

An ECHL Hall of Famer who coached teams to championships in the ECHL and AHL, Bednar had no NHL experience either as a player or coach when he was hired to replace Patrick Roy as head coach ahead of the 2016-17 season.

The Avs won 22 games in Bednar's first season as head coach, a finish that allowed the franchise to select Cale Makar with the fourth pick of the 2017 draft.

Colorado has qualified for the playoffs in every season since, including three straight trips to the second round ahead of the team's championship run in 2022.

Over that span Bednar has been at the helm for the development of some of the best players in the NHL in Makar, Nathan MacKinnon and former Avalanche star Mikko Rantanen.

The Avalanche are now coming off a franchise-record 121-point regular-season followed by the team's deepest playoff push since the Cup season, although the run ended with a conference finals sweep by the Vegas Golden Knights.

Sakic already showed his belief in the Avalanche's current stars by signing Makar to an extension currently set to make him the highest-paid player in the NHL.

The new contract for Bednar is another sign of faith this core can help the Avs compete for another Stanley Cup in the immediate future.

Bednar, 54, boasts a 445-262-75 regular-season record and 60-40-1 mark in the playoffs. He is the second-longest tenured coach in the NHL behind the Tampa Bay Lightning's Jon Cooper.

articles.title: WWE, AEW Rumors on LA Knight Heel Turn, Will Ospreay Blasting WWE and Steven Borden Injury Update
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

WWE Reportedly Not Interested in Knight Heel Turn

Despite speculation on how it could fit into the storyline, a heel turn reportedly isn't likely in the cards for LA Knight.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), WWE decision-makers "don't wanna" turn Knight heel, largely because of the hugely positive babyface reactions he routinely receives.

Knight is in the midst of a rivalry with Roman Reigns, and he is set to challenge The Tribal Chief for the World Heavyweight Championship at Money in the Bank on Oct. 10.

A central part of Knight's character in recent years has been his disdain for Reigns and The Bloodline, making him the perfect person to attempt to put an end to The OTC's run of dominance.

While Reigns has not been heavily involved in it, his Bloodline brethren have been embroiled in a heated feud with 946, who just added Jaida Parker to their group on Raw this week.

After kidnapping Solo Sikoa last week, 946 took out Jacob Fatu this week, as Parker hit him with her vehicle.

Given that 946 has been so heavily committed to destroying The Bloodline, there has been some online speculation that Knight could be the one pulling the strings.

While it would be a great storyline twist and a potential way to put the world title on Knight, it would be understandably tough for WWE to turn its back on the connection Knight clearly has with the viewing audience.

WWE Reportedly Not Dissuaded by Ospreay's Comments

People within WWE were reportedly not impacted by AEW world champion Will Ospreay's comments following All Out on Saturday night.

After Ospreay beat Jon Moxley in the All Out main event to retain his title, he offered a word of warning to WWE about attempts to counter-program AEW.

"Anytime anyone wants to come and step up to us, here's reality for you: we're gonna knock you down two f--king levels," Ospreay told reporters. "We are the best pro wrestling in the entire f--king world. Do not f--king step to us ever again."

All Out was held at Now Arena in the Chicago suburb of Hoffman Estates. However, at the same time, WWE ran its Worlds Collide show in the nearby Chicago suburb of Rosemont at Allstate Arena.

While WWE did draw more fans at an arena with a higher capacity, AEW still sold all 9,456 tickets it released, per WrestleTix .

Ospreay's words and AEW's successful night are reportedly not expected to deter WWE from similar actions in the future, though.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), WWE's reaction to Ospreay saying to not "step to" AEW again is, "Well, we're going to, time and time again."

WrestleVotes added that last weekend in Chicago was only the "beginning" of WWE running head-to-head with AEW.

While WWE has held events on the same night as AEW pay-per-views on multiple occasions, last weekend marked a change in philosophy in that WWE decided to run an event in the same town and at the same time as an AEW show.

Worlds Collide did not air live, but it will stream Wednesday night on YouTube, head-to-head with AEW Dynamite.

WWE has yet to shy away from competition with AEW, and it sounds like that will continue to be the case moving forward.

Injury Update on Steven Borden After All Out

Positive updates have emerged regarding Steven Borden's health following a scary spot Saturday at AEW All Out.

During a tag team match pitting Borden and Darby Allin against Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher, Borden and Knight spring-boarded into each other, but Borden had a rough landing, as he appeared to hit the back of his head on the mat.

After being checked by the referee and a doctor, the decision was made to call off the match at that point.

Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats) reported that Borden is "okay," and that he heard Borden was going to be able to fly home from Chicago.

That comes after AEW president Tony Khan told reporters following All Out that Borden was "awake and responsive," at the hospital, and that "all the tests have come back good."

Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful (h/t Mrosko ) added that if Borden continues to recover at his current rate, he could return to the ring within the next few weeks.

Borden, who is the son of legendary pro wrestler Sting, began his wrestling career late last year.

He has less than 40 career matches to his credit, and the vast majority of them have been dark matches wrestled prior to episodes of Dynamite and Collision.

All Out was unquestionably the biggest match of his career to date, and although it didn't go according to plan, every indication is that Borden is on the road to recovery.

articles.title: WWE's Roman Reigns Details Diet, Workout Plans, 'I Think I'm in My Prime Physically'
articles.summary: WWE world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns offered a glimpse this week into the preparation that goes into being one of the biggest stars in professional wrestling.
articles.body:
WWE world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns offered a glimpse this week into the preparation that goes into being one of the biggest stars in professional wrestling.

In an interview with Ebenezer Samuel of Men's Health , Reigns gave some insight into his diet, workouts and everything that goes into staying at the top of his game.

Despite being 41 years old and having been under a WWE contract since 2010, Reigns expressed his belief that he is better now than ever before from a physical perspective.

"I think I'm in my prime physically," Reigns said. "I look at my stomach or whatever it may be, that's a part of that body dysmorphia we're all struggling with. And it's one of those deals that I think if you just keep working on it…it's not done until it's done."

Reigns continued by revealing what he tells himself when he's going through struggles in terms of not necessarily being exactly where he wants to be physically.

"It's a marathon," Reigns said. "It's not over. Even if your goal is tomorrow, just extend it. Just keep going. If my look isn't perfect on Sunday, then I should probably just keep trying to make it a little better. Keep working at it."

For Reigns, discipline is everything, although he admitted that staying on the right track with his diet can be a challenge at times.

"If I get out of that, I can be the opposite, where I don't want to work out and I want to eat the worst stuff," Reigns said. "I want to order the food in. Is it 5:00 somewhere? Because I'd like to have a beer, too. It's one of those things that I have to be very careful about, and I have to constantly remind myself of what we're doing, what our goals are, and what we're trying to achieve."

While Reigns has a ripped physique, Samuel noted that there are many times when Reigns lifts lighter weights rather than doing some of the heavier lifts he did during his football days.

Reigns stressed the importance of being well-rounded in the sense of looking strong, but also having the athleticism and flexibility to perform in the ring.

"The crossover is huge, because we want to look like we can save the world," Reigns said. "There's that fine balance, where you want to look that part. But if that movement, that physicality, that athleticism is not there, it will take people out. [The audience] won't be able to get lost. There will be no escapism.

"That's the most important thing about being well-rounded. You can see when guys have a super strength over here, but then there's a deficit here. But then they're good here, but they don't have all the tools sharpened. It's important to have both those tools."

In addition to his work in WWE, Reigns had to tailor his diet and workouts to playing the role of Akuma in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, which is set for an Oct. 16 release.

Other wrestlers such as The Rock, John Cena and Batista have successfully transitioned from wrestling to acting, and it is fair to wonder if Reigns could be next in line.

However, for now, Reigns seems to still be fully committed to wrestling as the world champion and face of WWE, especially as he gets ready for his title defense against LA Knight at Money in the Bank on Oct. 10.

articles.summary: ¿Cuándo entregan el nuevo estadio El Campín? Revelan fecha oficial y plazos de la obra en Bogotá
articles.body: El megaproyecto de infraestructura deportiva y cultural de la capital entra en una nueva etapa. La Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá confirmó el ajuste en el cronograma oficial de las obras del nuevo estadio El Campín. El alcalde de Bogotá, Carlos Fernando Galán, junto con la concesión Sencia, anunció la reprogramación para la finalización del nuevo escenario deportivo. Aunque inicialmente se tenía previsto entregar la estructura terminada en diciembre de 2027, la nueva fecha de entrega oficial quedó fijada para diciembre de 2028. Esta modificación de 12 meses responde principalmente a los ajustes en la fase previa y la aprobación de los Planes de Manejo de Tránsito (PMT) e impacto en la movilidad, fundamentales para garantizar que las obras no colapsen la red vial de la zona. Con este anuncio, Bogotá asegura el desarrollo de un complejo multidisciplinario de talla internacional, adaptando los plazos de construcción a las exigencias urbanísticas de la capital.

articles.title: Sigue el 'boom' del pádel en los Estados Unidos: llega una nueva liga universitaria de la mano de Bela
articles.standfirst: La leyenda argentina impulsa el crecimiento de este deporte en el mercado estadounidense a través de los centros académicos
articles.summary: La leyenda argentina impulsa el crecimiento de este deporte en el mercado estadounidense a través de los centros académicos
articles.body: El pádel continúa su proceso de globalización y da un salto estratégico en su expansión dentro del mercado de Estados Unidos. En un país donde la estructura del deporte universitario forma la base del sistema deportivo, la disciplina entra en este ámbito de la mano de Fernando Belasteguín. El exjugador argentino mantiene su vinculación con este deporte tras su retirada de las pistas a finales de 2024. Desde entonces, ha ejercido como embajador de Wilson en diversos proyectos, dirige el P1 de Miami y gestiona el Bela Padel Center, que cuenta con sede central en Barcelona e instalaciones en distintos puntos internacionales. Belasteguín asume ahora el rol de embajador y asesor principal de la primera competición académica de esta disciplina en territorio estadounidense: la Wilson ACPL by Bela. La liga nace con la participación de 30 centros y 200 estudiantes repartidos en cuatro regiones. La competición dará comienzo en octubre y celebrará sus finales nacionales en el mes de marzo. En Estados Unidos, el pádel ha experimentado un crecimiento paulatino en convivencia con modalidades de alta implantación como el pickleball. El número de practicantes y de instalaciones ha registrado un incremento sostenido, con especial incidencia en zonas como Florida y Nueva York. A nivel profesional, el país acoge también eventos del circuito Pro Padel League y exhibiciones como la Reserve Cup. La puesta en marcha de un circuito universitario introduce al pádel en la estructura de formación deportiva norteamericana. Este modelo plantea además la posibilidad futura de que deportistas internacionales accedan a programas de becas académicas y deportivas en universidades estadounidenses, de forma análoga a lo que sucede en disciplinas como el tenis o el fútbol. La implicación de Belasteguín junto al patrocinio de la firma Wilson aporta respaldo técnico e institucional a un proyecto que busca consolidar la práctica del pádel a nivel formativo y competitivo en el país.

articles.title: Did Titans offer Derrick Henry free agent contract in 2023? Ravens RB says 'not at all'
articles.summary: Derrick Henry said he knew the Titans were ready to move on from him in his last season in Tennessee.
articles.body:
Derrick Henry described his departure from the Tennessee Titans to Baltimore media after the 2023 season on Sept. 30 by saying, "They shipped me out."

After a couple of seconds, the Titans' second-leading all-time rusher changed his tone.

"Nah, I mean don't want to say it like that," Henry said. "There's always love. But no, they didn't offer, not at all."

The subject naturally came up with Henry, 32, now in his third season with the Baltimore Ravens (2-1), preparing to face the Titans (0-3) in Baltimore on Oct. 4.

It wasn't the first time Henry said he didn't receive an offer to stay with the Titans after he became a free agent. It was reported in 2023 that the Titans rejected a trade offer from the Ravens for Henry for a fourth-round draft pick with contingencies to make it a third-round pick. Henry then left Tennessee after the season without an offer to stay.

On Sept. 30, Henry called his departure from Tennessee "bittersweet," adding that he knew before it was official that his time with the Titans was nearing an end in 2023.

"I knew the writing was on the wall throughout that season and they were ready to move on," Henry said. "You know, good things don't last forever, so it was time for me to find a new home ... and I knew what I wanted that home to be and it was here and so, God is good."

Henry rushed for 9,502 yards and 90 touchdowns with the Titans from 2016-2023. In 2024, he rushed for 1,921 yards and 16 touchdowns in Baltimore, and in 2025 he rushed for 1,595 yards and 16 touchdowns.

Henry heads into the game against the Titans with 301 yards on 61 carries and six touchdowns.

His replacement at Tennessee, Tony Pollard , rushed for more than 1,000 yards in each of the last two seasons but only 10 total touchdowns. Pollard had 173 yards on 38 carries and no touchdowns in 2026.

articles.title: Mets Lose Pitcher With 2.97 ERA In Minor Leagues This Year To Free Agency
articles.summary: The New York Mets missed the postseason for the second straight year this year
articles.body:
The New York Mets have a very important offseason ahead of them.

The Mets cannot start making impactful additions just yet, but that does not mean transactions around the league are at a halt. While big-league free agents won't hit the open market until after the World Series, eligible minor league players can elect free agency right now.

Kevin Herget elected free agency from the Mets on Tuesday. Herget only threw one inning for the Mets in the big leagues this season, but pitched in 19 minor league games for the Mets. He pitched in Triple-A, High-A, Single-A and the Florida Complex League.

He had a 2.97 ERA with 25 strikeouts in the minor leagues. He made eight starts and threw a total of 33 1/3 innings. Herget has a 4.13 career ERA in the big leagues and has pitched in 32 games. He is 35 years old and still has not established himself as a big leaguer.

He was drafted in 2013 and made his MLB debut in 2022. He may be the best signing in an international league like the KBO or NPB. It's possible a different team takes a chance on him or sees him as minor league depth, but overall, losing him is not a huge loss for the Mets.

articles.title: Breaking: Mardela softball coach Kory Shiles steps down after 21 years
articles.summary: Mardela announced that head softball coach Kory Shiles is stepping down after 21 years of coaching. Shiles' teams won state titles in 2025 and 2026.
articles.body:
Kory Shiles, the head softball coach at Mardela High School, is stepping down from his position after more than two decades coaching the team.

It was announced on Wednesday afternoon that Shiles would be stepping down as head coach of Mardela's softball team after 21 years of coaching. Shiles said that the reasoning behind his retirement as head softball coach is to spend more time coaching and watching his kids' sporting events at the high school, travel and youth levels.

"I take great pride in the impact our program has made on the game of softball and the Mardela community," Shiles said in a statement. "Those memories will last a lifetime, but I'm most proud of taking our little one stoplight town on the Eastern Shore of Maryland and turning it into one of the best softball programs in the state of Maryland and recognized as one of the top small-town teams in the USA."

During his time coaching Mardela softball, Shiles won back-to-back MPSSAA Class 1A State Championships in 2025 and 2026, the first state titles in Mardela's softball history since 1980. His Warriors teams also won 11 Bayside South division titles, six Bayside Conference Championships, and eight regional championships. Shiles won 350 games in his head coaching career with the Warriors.

"Coach Kory Shiles has made an incredible impact on Mardela High School, both on and off the softball field," Mardela Principal Liza Hastings said in a statement. "For years, he has helped young women develop not only as athletes, but as leaders, teammates and confident individuals. His dedication, passion and commitment to our students have helped shape generations of Warriors. We are grateful for his service and wish him the very best in retirement."

articles.title: See it: J.J. McCarthy in a New York Giants uniform for first time
articles.summary: Watch New York Giants QB J.J. McCarthy practice in Big Blue's uniform for the first time.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy practiced in a New York Giants uniform for the first time on Wednesday, two days after New York acquired the quarterback from the Minnesota Vikings .

Video from the session showed McCarthy in a red No. 18 jersey, taking snaps and working around teammates that included running back Cam Skattebo.

The 23-year-old had worn No. 9 at Michigan and throughout his Vikings tenure, but that number already belongs to tight end Isaiah Likely . The Giants assigned McCarthy No. 18 after the trade.

That jersey previously belonged to Jake Haener . New York waived Haener on Monday to open a roster spot for McCarthy, then re-signed him to the practice squad. Haener is now wearing No. 13, the number Odell Beckham Jr. had reclaimed this season before his release.

McCarthy arrived after starter Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. Jameis Winston is expected to start Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals while McCarthy works into John Harbaugh's offense. The 10th overall pick in 2024 completed 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 10 games with Minnesota.

The first look in Giants colors is only a starting point. McCarthy's next step is earning a role in a quarterback room that changed quickly over the past week.

articles.title: Ohio State Week 5 Preview: Sayin, Smith, And Who Else?
articles.summary: Ohio State has a test this weekend at the ever-dangerous Kinnick Stadium. Can the offense keep it rolling against a better defense?
articles.body:
Ohio State is set to travel to Kinnick Stadium for the first time since 2017 ( drink ), and will do so wearing their all-while iteration of the standard road uniforms. The Buckeye offense looked good last week against Illinois thanks to force-feeding the best player in college football. However, Iowa's defense is set to be a bit more difficult to move the ball on compared to Illinois's.

The second matchup in the Big Ten on the Buckeyes' schedule is a good one, especially since Iowa went into Michigan and beat the Wolverines. Now, the Hawkeyes are ranked the highest they've been since the 2021 season (remember when Iowa was ranked number two??). Let's take a look at what the Buckeye offense can do to get to 2-0 in the Big Ten.

Ohio State Week 5 Preview: Sayin, Smith, And Who Else?

For as storied a career Jeremiah Smith has put together to this point, last weekend was a high point. He essentially beat the Fighting Illini single-handedly, scoring four touchdowns as Illinois only managed 19 points itself. He already owns the Ohio State career record for yards and is the only Buckeye receiver to ever eclipse 3,000 yards.

After that monster performance, he's just 10 receptions and two touchdowns away from owning the Ohio State triple crown of records. Iowa should present a stiffer challenge, but there is certainly a timeline in which Smith owns all three records by the time 00:00 is left on the clock. The offense goes through him, as it should. The rushing attack hasn't been there (more on that later), but Smith is good enough to carry the offense if need be. Expect another concerted effort to get him the ball.

If you're looking toward the Big Ten records, they're still quite lofty. Tayler Stubblefield (Purdue) racked up 325 receptions between 2001 and 2004. Smith is 130 away from owning the record. John Standeford (Purdue) amassed 3,788 yards from 2000 through 2003. Smith is now 614 yards away. Finally, Braylon Edwards (Michigan) owns the Big Ten record for receiving touchdowns with 39, and Smith is just six scores away.

Receptions may be difficult, but the other two marks should be squarely within reach, especially if the Buckeyes reach the Big Ten Championship and play in a couple College Football Playoff games. Side note: Imagine if Smith played as many games as Stubblefield, Standeford, and Edwards; those records would be untouchable. Alas, the NFL beckons after this year.

Either way, Iowa is up next, and Smith put up 89 yards and a ridiculous one-handed touchdown on four receptions in his only matchup with the Hawkeyes back in 2024.

Last week, the Buckeyes didn't allow a single sack. Finally, a bold prediction that ends up correct! Of course, keeping Julian Sayin upright against Iowa will be a bit harder.

Ohio State got a Super Saiyan performance out of its quarterback, but it was overshadowed by its top receiver going Ultra Instinct. Again, Sayin leads the Big Ten in completion percentage despite a disappointing showing against Texas. He's still rolling with a completion percentage over 75% in his career, so that career record is still in reach. More impressively, he's averaging over 300 yards per game, leading the Big Ten. If he keeps this up, he's going to blow last year's numbers out of the water. We may have some Heisman voters splitting their ballots.

Again, the question will have to be: who is going to step up beside Smith? Sayin has 83 completions, 1,206 yards, and 10 touchdowns thus far this year; Smith has 33 receptions, 607 yards, and seven touchdowns. The next closest is Devin McCuin with 13 receptions for 165 yards and one touchdown. Chris Henry Jr. has three receptions this year…for two touchdowns.

It looked like Nate Roberts is a bit more incorporated into the offense, so that'll be something to watch. Also, Brandon Inniss – what happened last week? The senior finished without a catch for the first time since Week 3 of last year.

Smith and Sayin can carry the offense, but it would unlock an entirely different level of efficiency and explosiveness if defenses had to plan for another threat. Maybe when Kyle Parker gets healthy, he can be that guy?

Part of the issue causing the offense to be "Jeremiah Smith down there somewhere" is the fact that the rushing attack can't get going. Is it the running backs? Is it the offensive line? It's likely a mixture of both.

Sure, the offensive line has had a few injuries, causing a jumbling of the lineup. But the run game isn't there. The explosiveness isn't there, and when the Buckeyes need a few yards, it's difficult unless Sayin decides to take it himself.

Much has been made about the lack of Legend Bey in the offense. It's a fair criticism, especially when Bo Jackson , Ja'Kobi Jackson , and Isaiah West are struggling. Bo Jackson is still the lead man with just under six yards per carry, but the chunk plays haven't been there. That's where Bey allegedly fits in.

Coaches rave about his athleticism. Scouts who watched him in high school repeatedly mention how explosive he is. From the outside looking in, it looks like he's a bit in the doghouse, whether still due to those poorly executed kickoff returns against Ball State or something else. In total, he played one snap against Texas (a blown-up toss run) and three against Kent State. He left that Kent State with a lower-body injury, but didn't appear on the availability report last week, so his not playing had to have been a coaching decision.

It feels like a broken record from The Fringe at this point, but if you want to see what you've got, you have to play him.

Iowa is coming off an emotional, last-second win over Michigan. Who knows how they respond. If we know anything about Kirk Ferentz, it's that he will have his team ready to go.

Iowa has the best scoring defense in the nation, allowing just eight points per game through four weeks. That is thanks to two shutouts of Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa, of course. Against Iowa State and Michigan, the Hawkeyes allowed 13 and 19 points, respectively. Of course, that's still pretty good.

If there is an area to attack, it's the secondary. Michigan and their anemic passing attack managed 276 yards and two touchdowns through the air. Sure, the Hawkeyes don't have to respect Sayin's legs to the level they had to do with Bryce Underwood, but Sayin's arm should more than make up for that. Also, if you're hoping the run game gets figured out this week, you may be disappointing. Iowa is allowing 2.7 yards per carry this year (3.9 yards per carry against those two Power 4 programs).

As usual, Iowa has solid linebackers in Jayden Montgomery and Cam Buffington, so keep them in mind.

Where : Kinnick Stadium, Iowa City, Iowa History : Ohio State 48-15-3 Iowa (2010 win vacated) Last Matchup : Ohio State won, 35-7, in 2024 Last Illinois Win: 55-24 in 2017 Date and Time : 3:30 p.m. ET How to Watch : CBS Spread : Ohio State -14.5; O/U 45.5 (via FanDuel)

Prediction : Ohio State fell short of covering the spread for the first time last week. That shouldn't be the case this week. Ohio State should be at least two scores better than Iowa, Kinnick voodoo or not. The defense will have moments of struggle, but the offense should force the Iowa game plan into throwing the ball early. Buckeyes win, 35-17.

articles.title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Issues Strong Drake Maye Statement
articles.summary: The New England Patriots and head coach Mike Vrabel enter Week 4 trying to figure out their slow start to the 2026 NFL season. After losing to the Jacksonvil...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots and head coach Mike Vrabel enter Week 4 trying to figure out their slow start to the 2026 NFL season. After losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week in blowout fashion by a final score of 35-6, the team currently sits at 1-2.

Last season, Vrabel led the Patriots to the Super Bowl. They came up short against the Seattle Seahawks , but the future looked incredibly bright. Drake Maye was a top-tier MVP candidate and appeared ready to take the leap into superstardom this year.

Maye has struggled to begin his third NFL season.

Vrabel has been taking a lot of heat due to the slow start this season for New England . Maye has taken an equal amount of heat.

With that being said, the head coach spoke out on Wednesday with a strong statement about his young quarterback. Vrabel clearly remains confident that the Patriots can get things turned around this season.

Patriots' Mike Vrabel Makes Telling Drake Maye Statement

When asked about a local report that he and Maye have some kind of issue with each other, Vrabel didn't hold back. He put an end to those rumblings quickly.

"Unnamed sources? Let me just tell you why I'm here," Vrabel said . "I'm here because Drake was the QB. Believe it or not, I had choices to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here because Drake was the QB."

Needless to say, Maye has the full support of his head coach. The start to this season may not be going as planned, but the head coach and quarterback are still very clearly on the same page.

Through the first three games of the season, Maye has completed 63.7 percent of his pass attempts for 585 yards, a touchdown, and six interceptions. He has been a turnover machine and hasn't been able to put points up on the scoreboard.

While there are obviously reasons to be concerned about the bad start to the year, New England has time to turn things around. No team is done after just three weeks. Vrabel and Maye made a run to the Super Bowl last season and deserve to be given more time to right the ship.

Next up for the Patriots will be a Week 4 matchup on the road against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills . That will be a very tough game for New England. However, a road win over the Bills could be exactly what the Patriots need to get back on track.

articles.title: Red Wings' Simon Edvinsson heads to Sweden as he awaits new contract
articles.summary: Simon Edvinsson, a restricted free agent without a contract, has returned home and was skating with a Swedish team in his hometown of Gothenburg.
articles.body:
Players can't wait to welcome back their teammate, even as he has distanced himself from the Detroit Red Wings.

News broke out of Sweden on Wednesday, Sept. 30 that Simon Edvinsson , a restricted free agent without a contract, had returned home and was skating with Fröulunda in his hometown of Gothenburg. He last skated iwth the Red Wings Saturday morning, before their final preseason game.

"We just know that he wants to be here," teammate Moritz Seider said after practice. "We want him here, and that's the bottom line. Everyone has to fight for their own contracts, and we all have his back and we support him. And we're just looking forward to when he eventually signs, hopefully sooner rather than late because he's a big part of our team, a big part of this organization and, moving forward, he will be a big piece to our success."

Swedish reporter Andreas III Johansson posted on social media that, "Simon Edvinsson is back in Sweden. Training with Frölunda on Wednesday."

Edvinsson, 23, arranged for his own insurance so he could be with his teammates during training camp, taking part in practices but not scrimmages or exhibition games. Once the preseason ended, however, he was no longer around the team. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said in a statement, "Simon is not practicing with the team. The organization will continue conversations with Simon and his representatives."

The Red Wings open the 2026-27 season on Friday, Oct. 2, when they host the New York Rangers . Edvinsson could make the opener if he's signed in the next 24 hours, though it would require an early morning flight from Sweden connecting through a major international airport like Amsterdam Schipol airport or Paris Charles De Gaulle.

"The situation is an important one, but we have so much to worry about in here," forward Andrew Copp said. "I can't really worry about if Simon is going to be here Friday or not. That's not my job. We want Simon here. He's a fantastic player, he's going to be a huge player for us for a long time, but none of us can control whether he's going to be here Friday or not."

Two years ago, under former general manager Steve Yzerman, then-RFAs Seider and Lucas Raymond did not sign new deals until right around the start of camp.

"I think as a teammate, you're making sure that he's in a good mindset," Raymond said. "You kind of let all the business side to the front office. That's all we can do. Simon's a great player. He's a great guy. He's a big part of our team and we want him here. But at the same time, that's not really in our control. We're focused on Friday."

If Edvinsson isn't available, rookie Anton Johansson looks poised to make his debut.

"The players that are here in the locker room, the coaching staff that's here, we have jobs to do," coach Todd McLellan said. "The business between Simon and the hockey club, we have nothing to do with it. We can't change it. We can't affect it. There's nothing we can do about it. So it's pretty simple − we get out, we have a good practice like we did today, and we get ready for the game. And if you're in a Red Wing jersey, then you're playing. That's the only way we can deal with it."

articles.title: Steelers rule Joey Porter Jr. out for Thursday, Jalen Ramsey questionable
articles.summary: Porter will miss his fourth straight game.
articles.body:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appeared to be making progress toward a return to the Steelers lineup this week, but any hope he would make his 2026 debut on Thursd night against the Browns has been dashed.

Porter was ruled out by the Steelers on Wednesday. Porter was listed as a full participant in practice on Monday and Tuesday with conditioning work given as the only reason why he was on the list. He was limited on Wednesday, however, and the back injury that kept him on the physically unable to perform list all summer is back on the report as well.

While the back injury and need for conditioning are the health reasons for Porter's absence, his inability to secure a contract extension has been the backdrop to the weekly questions about his availability and the one step forward, one step back nature of his practice work does little to suggest that the contract isn't playing a role.

The Steelers have other injury concerns at corner. Jalen Ramsey is listed as questionable with what he said is a broken wrist and Brandin Echols has the same designation due to a concussion.

Running back Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out for the second straight game.

articles.title: Avalanche give coach Jared Bednar new contract, avoid lame-duck season
articles.summary: The Colorado Avalanche have agreed to terms on a contract extension for coach Jared Bednar before the start of the 2026-27 NHL season.
articles.body:
The Colorado Avalanche and longtime coach Jared Bednar have agreed on a four-year contract extension, the team announced on Wednesday, Sept. 30, and avoided an awkward lame-duck situation ahead of the start to its 2026-27 NHL season .

Bednar was entering the final year of his deal but is now signed through the 2030-31 campaign. He led the Avalanche to a franchise-record 121 points and the Presidents' Trophy last season before a Stanley Cup playoff run to the Western Conference Finals, where Colorado was swept by the Las Vegas Golden Knights .

Bednar, 54, just completed his 10th season as coach of the franchise, where he won the Stanley Cup title in 2022.

NHL players who changed teams in the offseason

"Jared has done an outstanding job over the last decade, and there's no doubt in my mind he's the best coach for this group," Avalanche President of Hockey Operations and General Manager Joe Sakic said in a statement. "He commands the room and has complete confidence of the players. We're excited to continue to have him in charge, and we believe that his presence maximizes the team's potential while this core group is intact."

Bednar is the winningest coach in franchise history with a career record of 445-262-75 and the second-longest tenured coach in the NHL. Terms of his new contract were not disclosed.

The Avalanche have reached the playoffs in all but one season during his decade with the franchise. They open the 2026-27 season against the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday.

"I'm extremely happy and grateful to continue leading this group," said Bednar. "My family and I have loved being a part of this organization from the beginning, and I can't thank the Kroenke family and Joe Sakic enough for their support. I look forward to working hard each day this season and beyond to accomplish our goal of winning another Stanley Cup."

articles.title: Panthers HC Dave Canales provides bittersweet update on CBs Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson
articles.summary: Panthers HC Dave Canales put a rough timeline on the potential returns of CBs Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers may not have lost their two starting cornerbacks for the season, but they will have to wait a while to see if they can get them back.

On Wednesday, the team placed Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve—sidelining the standout duo for at least the next four weeks. Horn, in Carolina's Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns , sustained a " significant " quad tear while Jackson went down with a groin injury.

Unfortunately, the two will be out for quite a bit longer than that four-week minimum—as noted by head coach Dave Canales following today's practice.

"Neither of them are out for the season," Canales told reporters this afternoon. "I'll give you kinda a rough timeline—it's like eight-ish weeks, give or take. Could be sooner, could be longer. So it's a big swing there depending on how the return-to-play process goes with both guys."

Canales later added that Jackson underwent a successful surgery on Tuesday. Horn, meanwhile, will not undergo a procedure and entered right into rehab.

With Horn and Jackson out, the Panthers are expected—at least for the time being—to start 2026 fourth-round pick Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans in their places.

articles.title: Vikings announce latest update on Justin Jefferson after missing practice
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings had the latest update on wide receiver Justin Jefferson.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are taking a cautious approach with Justin Jefferson as the star wide receiver works his way back from an ankle injury.

Jefferson did not practice Wednesday ahead of Minnesota's Week 4 matchup with the Miami Dolphins . ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Vikings consider Jefferson day-to-day with the injury.

That designation comes just days after Jefferson left Minnesota's 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He suffered the ankle injury during the opening drive and did not return after catching two passes for 32 yards.

The Vikings received encouraging news after further testing. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Jefferson has an ankle sprain but avoided anything long-term.

Jefferson's absence from Wednesday's practice does not necessarily rule him out for Sunday. Minnesota still has several days to see how he responds before making a final decision on his status.

The timing is important for an undefeated Vikings team. Minnesota improved to 3-0 with the win over Tampa Bay and will return home to face a Dolphins team that entered Week 4 at 0-3.

Jefferson has been productive when healthy this season. Through three games, he has 13 receptions for 179 yards and two touchdowns.

Dec 21, 2025; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) makes a catch against the New York Giants during the first half at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images

His absence in Tampa Bay also showed how quickly Minnesota's offense can lose one of its biggest weapons. Jefferson played only a handful of snaps before the ankle injury ended his afternoon.

The Vikings now have to balance the short-term goal of staying unbeaten with the need to make sure Jefferson is ready for the long season ahead.

For now, Jefferson is day-to-day and did not practice Wednesday. His participation over the next two days should provide a better indication of whether he can play against Miami.

articles.title: Qua Moss named to Paul Hornung Award Honor Roll after Texas game

articles.body:
Tennessee senior defensive back and return specialist Qua Moss was named to the Paul Hornung Award Honor Roll after Week 4.

He received the honor following his performance in Tennessee's, 20-17, loss to No. 1 Texas on Sept. 26 at Neyland Stadium. Moss recorded five tackles and one pass breakup.

On special teams, he returned three punts, including one for a 57-yard touchdown that tied the Tennessee- Texas game, 10-10.

Through four games this season, Moss has totaled 16 tackles, two tackles for a loss, one pass breakup, 95 punt return yards and one punt return touchdown. He ranks fourth in the SEC, averaging 13.6 yards per punt return.

Moss transferred to Tennessee from Kansas State after the 2025 football season.

The Paul Hornung Award, presented annually by the Louisville Sports Commission, recognizes the most versatile player in college football. The honor recognizes players who demonstrate excellence in multiple facets of the game.

articles.title: Guardians Should Pull the Don Mattingly Move… But Do it Better
articles.summary: Don't be afraid to be bold
articles.body:
Some controversy around Don Mattingly's use of his closer in yesterday's NL Wildcard game vs. the Braves should provide some opportunity for conversation for the Guardians leading into their American League Division Series beginning this weekend.

Entering the bottom of the seventh inning with a 3-2 lead, Mattingly brought Jhoan Duran in to face numbers 9, 1 and 2 in the Atlanta Braves ' order. He then brought him out again in the eighth to get hitters 3, 4 and 5 in the order. The internet is now full of folks calling Mattingly's decision to go to his closer earlier a mistake because Duran ended up giving up a 3-run, go-ahead homer to Austin Riley in the 8th after the 5th and 6th hitters reach (via infield hit and a hit-by-pitch). But, I don't think that's quite fair to Mattingly… or to Duran… or to any team that might take a similar strategic path.

Duran came in with a narrow one-run lead and got five straight outs from the most dangerous hitters in the Atlanta lineup. He then gave up incredibly weak contact that unluckily resulted in a hit. At this point, someone should have been warming and getting ready as quickly as possible. Said pitcher would have had six pitches and a potential mound visit to start to get ready before the fateful Riley at-bat. However, I suspect Mattingly had a longer leash on Duran than optimal because the Phillies ' bullpen as a whole is not great.

I would argue that Mattingly' process – despite the bad result – was sound. The most important thing to do in a playoff game in which you have a lead in the 7th or later is make sure that your best reliever throws meaningful pitches against your opponent's best hitters. He accomplished this and got 5 out of 6 hitters out. At that point, I think it would have made sense to have the next best option ready to come in the game and remove Duran, not only because it was an unfamiliar situation for their closer but because there were two outs and you're asking for one more out with a runner on first. Additionally, no one other than the six hitters who have faced him gets a rep against Duran to help them later in the series (though Atlanta is very familiar with the Phillies).

I hope Stephen Vogt can have conversations with his bullpen about similar situations. If the Guardians had the exact same situation, going to Cade Smith there makes perfect sense and guarantees he sees the best hitters at the end of the game with a lead. Smith also has experience going multiple innings and being the "fireman" in the past. The off days of the series should also allow the Guardians to be aggressive with Smith and their other best arms as they will have time to recover in-between appearances. Erik Sabrowski , Daniel Espino , Shawn Armstrong , a healthy Colin Holderman and even on a good day Tim Herrin are more than capable of getting a batter to end the 8th… or you let Tanner Bibee or Foster Griffin throw the kitchen sink at a hitter.

I do not mean to dismiss the importance of reliever comfort and role establishment. If the team truly believes that Smith being jarred from the role of pitching the 8th into the 9th would negatively affect his mental status, don't do it. However, from everything we know of Cade, I doubt this is the case. The one thing to avoid at all costs is losing a lead in the 7th or later without Cade Smith facing your opponent's greatest threats. Mattingly made sure to avoid it yesterday and I hope the Guardians will as well in the series to come.

articles.title: Week 6 high school football preview: District 14-5A-II playoff chase heats up
articles.summary: Week 6 high school football preview: The District 14-5A-II playoff chase heats up.
articles.body:
A stormy forecast could put a damper on this weekend high school football schedule in San Antonio, including the Express-News Game of the Week between Kerrville Tivy and Davenport. With several district on open weeks, including 27-6A and 30-6A, it might be the best time for this to happen. As of Wednesday, this is how the other top games from Week 6 are scheduled:

Sam Houston vs. Lanier, 7 p.m. Thursday, SAISD Complex : The battle for the four playoff spots in District 14-5A-II appears tight and this game could decide a playoff spot. Sam Houston (3-2 overall) and Lanier (3-1) are tied for third in district at 2-1, one game behind co-leaders Harlandale and McCollum, both 3-0. Sam Houston bounced back from a tough 13-12 loss against McCollum two weeks ago to beat Edison, 26-14. Lanier's running game powered by Nicholas Torres (617 yards, nine touchdowns), Erick Esparza (495 yards, five touchdowns) and Isaiah (247 yards, one touchdown) could thrive under potentially sloppy conditions on the natural surface at SAISD Complex.

LEE vs. Roosevelt, 7 p.m. Thursday, Heroes Stadium: This is a "prove-it" game for both teams. After starting 3-0, LEE dropped its District 28-6A opener to No. 1 Johnson, 66-6. That's not a catastrophic loss. Johnson has breezed in all their victories. But, if the Volunteers want to get into the playoffs for the first time since 1993, a victory here would be ideal. No. 18 Roosevelt (2-2, 1-0) is aiming for its first playoff berth since 2020. A 2-0 start in league play gives them some cushion before playing Johnson next week. The Rough Riders have won two in a row since starting 0-2. They outlasted Madison in four overtimes, 45-43, last week in their league opener.

Harlandale vs. Jefferson, 7 p.m. Friday, Harlandale Memorial Stadium : Harlandale (3-2, 3-0 14-5A-II) is off to its best start in league play since 2005 when it went 6-0 and won the District 30-4A title. The Indians have posted district wins against Edison (27-7), Lanier (37-18) and Burbank (48-0) after going 0-2 in non-district. Senior quarterback Gabriel Salazar has passed for 562 yards and 11 touchdowns, and senior running back Gio Silva has 89 rushes for 564 yards and two scores. Jefferson (2-1, 1-1) opened district with a 31-14 loss against Lanier before defeating Burbank 29-21. The Mustangs have combined for 580 rushing yards and 101 passing yards in four games.

Warren vs. Sotomayor, 7:30 p.m. Friday, Gustafson Stadium : There's still a long way to go, but the District 29-6A race is controlled by No. 4 Brennan (4-1) and No. 10 Harlan (4-1) at the top with 3-0 league marks. Outside of that, it's a battle for the two remaining postseason spots. No. 17 Warren and Sotomayor sit tied for third place at 2-1 (each is 3-2 overall). O'Connor (1-1) is the only other team with one district loss. Warren is coming off a 34-13 victory against Taft backed by senior quarterback Mac Anderson and his four touchdown passes. It was a great way to respond after losing against Harlan 41-7. Sotomayor defeated winless Stevens 27-7 one week after losing against Brennan 49-0.

Floresville at Somerset, 7 p.m.: How good is Floresville? We should find out over the next two games. The No. 20 Tigers (4-1) are off to their best start since 2021. They haven't won four games in a season since 2020. They've won three in a row, including last week's District 14-4A-I opener against Kennedy 67-3. After Somerset, the Tigers take on No. 11 La Vernia (4-1), which is No. 6 in the Class 4A Division I state rankings. Somerset (2-2) opens district play after taking last week off. Adrian Buentello has passed for 557 yards and six touchdowns. Playmaking receiver Malakai Iverson has 15 catches for 267 yards and two scores. Somerset needs to guard against looking ahead with a road game against La Vernia looming next week.

Runners who love Taco Bell and ultramarathons could combine both in an upcoming competition in Colorado.

The ninth edition of the International Taco Bell 50k Ultramarathon is set to taje place Saturday in Denver, according to race organizers .

The 31-mile race, which is not sponsored or endorsed by Taco Bell, takes participants past 11 branches of the fast food franchise.
