Participants are required to eat during at least ten of the 11 stops, with mandatory menu items including either a Chalupa Supreme or Crunchwrap Supreme as well as a Burrito Supreme or Nachos Bell Grande.

The course must be completed in under 11 hours, and dietary aids including Pepto, Alka Sellzter and Mylanta are not allowed during the run, according to organizers.

The race also features two additional levels in the Diablo Challenge, in which participants are encouraged to "slather all items with Diablo sauce and do a Diablo shooter at the end," and the Baja Blast challenge, in which runners have to drink two liters of the soda without vomiting.

Race organizers note on the race's sign-up page "it is a good idea to engage in gastric training" before participation.

The race, which begins at 7:30 a.m. local time Sunday in Denver, has popped up in similar interactions across the United States. East Coast runners looking to join in on the experience could participate in a similar 50k the day after Thanksgiving in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: World Rally Championship: The five titles that got away as Elfyn Evans closes in on elusive crown
articles.summary: As Elfyn Evans looks to finally clinch the World Rally Championship title in Sardinia, BBC Sport looks back at the five times he finished runner-up.
articles.body:
Few leading sports stars have been so tantalisingly close to crowning glory for so long without achieving ultimate success as rally driver Elfyn Evans.

The 37-year-old from Dolgellau in north-west Wales has been runner-up in the World Rally Championship (WRC) five times in the past six years.

With this year's WRC calendar truncated by the removal of the planned Saudi Arabia finale, Evans takes a 17-point lead into the now season-ending Rally Italia Sardegna from 1-4 October.

If Evans can maintain his advantage over team-mates Sami Pajari and Oliver Solberg it will be a crowning moment for the Welshman, who would become only the third Briton to win the WRC title - joining Colin McRae and Richard Burns.

As he prepares to grasp history in Sardinia, BBC Sport looks back at the five times Evans fell just short of his dream.

No change for leader Evans after WRC drops finale

White, Netherlands, Evans and sport's other great runners-up

BBC to broadcast World Rally Championship from 2027

Evans does have a world title - winning the WRC Junior Championship in 2012 which earned him a full-time seat in M-Sport's Ford Fiesta.

However, it was a move to Toyota Gazoo Racing in 2020 that put his senior career into overdrive.

Only huge last-event misfortune cost him instant success in a season cut from 13 races to seven by the Covid-19 pandemic.

After placing third at Monte Carlo in his first Yaris outing, Evans and co-driver Scott Martin excelled at a weather-shortened second round to win Rally Sweden.

It put the Welshman top of the WRC driver's championship for the first time, and although record-breaking Sebastien Ogier would temporarily reclaim the lead, a second victory in Turkey saw Evans take at 14-point advantage over the Frenchman into the final event.

With 10 of the 16 stages complete, the less experienced of the two drivers remained on course for a maiden championship success.

But Evans' dream ended in devastating fashion when he crashed down a bank after being caught out by treacherous snow-covered mountain roads.

Ogier claimed a seventh world title by just eight points to leave his team-mate "gutted".

"When I braked on that, it was just like glass and there was no chance of us slowing down at all. It completely caught me by surprise," said Evans after the race, later admitting "it was a massive disappointment", which made him "more determined" for the year ahead.

Evans took that determination and experience into the new year and soon grabbed the lead in the season-opening Rallye Monte Carlo.

However, local favourite Ogier went on to win in Monaco, and then three more of the first six rounds to take a commanding grip of the 2021 championship.

By mid-August - with four rounds remaining and a deficit of 38 points - Evans conceded: "The gap is quite a big one now. We've got a real uphill struggle if we want to try and win the championship."

The Welsh driver was not about to give up though. A second rally win of the season in Finland. and second place in the penultimate round at Rally Catalunya, once again forced the title race into a final-event decider at Monza.

With a potentially bridgeable gap of 17 points, the two Toyota rally crews swapped the lead throughout - but Ogier and co-driver Julien Ingrassia eventually came out on top to claim both the rally and the title.

"It's been a pretty OK year," a typically level-headed Evans reflected at the end of the race.

"Of course, I can't help but feel a little disappointed right now, you always look to the places you could've done better."

The following year could certainly have been much better - as Evans struggled with the newly introduced hybrid cars.

Going off the road in the opening round and forced to retire from three further rallies, Evans finished 2022 in fourth place, more than 120 points behind first-time champion Kalle Rovanpera.

"2022 fell below our expectations," a defiant Evans told the BBC before the 2023 campaign.

"We're coming into the new season looking for improvements - and we're hoping we can challenge for the title."

And challenge he did - winning round four in Croatia to take a share of the championship lead, tied with Ogier and one point ahead of Rovanperra.

However, a crash at Rally Portugal set his title bid back as he was forced to retire in round five and - despite a victory in Finland - Evans had to concede the title with one round to go.

A crash and a disappointing finish at the Central European Rally may have handed back-to-back titles to Finnish team-mate Rovanpera, but the Welshman was to end the season on a high.

Victory at Rally Japan was his third of the campaign - the best return in any season to date for Evans who declared "it feels nice after last year".

With Rovanpera following Ogier's lead for 2024 in deciding not to contest a full calendar, surely this would be the year their Toyota team-mate would finally get to stand atop the WRC podium?

Sadly for Evans, the opening paragraph of the BBC report for the season's first race set the tone.

'Elfyn Evans faded to finish a disappointing third behind winner Thierry Neuville at Rallye Monte Carlo.'

As it turned out it was second place in the driver's championship come December, but it was another disappointing season for the Welsh driver, with Neuville instead becoming a first-time world champion after Evans' years of waiting.

And Evans, of course, was runner-up - though only just.

As Neuville lined up in Nagoya needing just six points - he collected 17 - to end his own streak of five championship runners-up spots, the Welshman began Rally Japan in third place.

For the second year in a row, Evans saved his best for last and a back-to-back Japanese victory brought a double silver lining.

Not only did it see him overhaul Ott Tanak to claim runners-up spot for a fourth time, it also saw Toyota snatch the manufacturer's championship.

However, the big personal prize remained as elusive as ever.

"We're sorry we couldn't deliver [the drivers'] championship," Evans said, "but we'll try again next year."

A revamp of the points system for 2025 was welcomed by Evans; it also brought his tightest title race yet.

After second place to Ogier in the Monte Carlo curtain-raiser, the re-energised Welshman won in Sweden and Kenya - rallies the Frenchman sat out.

With a 36-point advantage, Evans had opened up the largest championship lead ever recorded after three rounds of a WRC campaign.

But he would not win again that season and though he never finished lower than sixth, Ogier gradually whittled away at his lead until it came down to just three points with one round to go.

That race was a brand new entry to the calendar, and there was uncertainty over what lay ahead at Rally Saudi Arabia.

The terrain proved brutal for all the drivers. Tyre problems galore saw the leaderboard shifting like the sand. It ended with Ogier in third and Evans in sixth.

The points-swing was seven. The Frenchman had won a record-equalling ninth WRC title by four points, and Evans had fallen just short for the fifth time in six years.

"We've done what we can, that's it," was his reaction.

"We're competitors at the end of the day, we always want better, we always want more."

But there is only one more thing to do. Finally shake-off the tag of nearly-man.

He grabbed the 2026 championship lead with victory in February's Rally Sweden and has refused to let it go.

Once again his rivals are Toyota team-mates. This time it is Pajari, who won three rallies in a row, before Solberg triumphed in Rally Chile at the start of September to put himself back in the title reckoning.

Evans will require at most 19 points to guarantee him the title, but has not finished higher than third in the past five rallies since winning in Japan.

He will also have to cope with being first on the road in Sardinia - sweeping the gravel which has frequently caused him trouble in the past.

"I think especially with opening the road, normally in Sardinia it's a significant disadvantage to run first," concedes Evans who says he will "ignore the championship situation".

"You can't really afford to [think about the lead]. I have plenty of experience of what not to do," he muses.

"But you know how it turns out. I think it's far less certain than what it appears on paper."

True, but maybe by Sunday, the paper in the history books will show Evans finally proved he is not just another runner-up.

articles.title: Manolo Lama desvela las presiones que recibía en GOL: "Nunca retiramos nada"
articles.standfirst: El periodista recuerda en Otra Ronda de Radio MARCA su etapa en la ya desaparecida cadena
articles.summary: El periodista recuerda en Otra Ronda de Radio MARCA su etapa en la ya desaparecida cadena
articles.body: Manolo Lama fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de la historia de GOL TV. El periodista lideró durante años El Golazo de GOL, un informativo deportivo que se convirtió en una de las señas de identidad de la cadena. Ahora, tras conocerse el final de esta etapa, Lama ha pasado por Radio MARCA, en Otra Ronda, para recordar aquellos años y hablar de las circunstancias que rodearon el final del canal. El periodista fue contundente al analizar la desaparición de GOL TV y reconoció que el desenlace no le sorprendió. "Yo creo que evidentemente era una muerte anunciada. Buscaron que el canal se fuera muriendo poquito a poquito", aseguró. Lama explicó que el equipo ya intuía cuál podía ser el destino de la cadena, aunque mantuvo el compromiso hasta el último momento: "Nosotros hasta el último día, hasta el último segundo del último programa, lo dimos todo". Uno de los aspectos más llamativos de la entrevista fue cuando habló de las presiones que recibían desde algunos clubes. Lama reconoció que eran habituales, especialmente cuando el programa emitía imágenes que podían resultar incómodas para determinadas entidades. "Cada vez que sacábamos una imagen dolorosa para algún club automáticamente llamaban para que tratáramos de retirarla", explicó. Sin embargo, aseguró que el equipo no cedió ante esas peticiones: "Tengo que decir que nunca, nunca, nunca retiramos nada". Lama puso como ejemplo a varios de los grandes clubes españoles. "Nos retiraron la palabra a nosotros, pues el Barça, el Madrid, que se recuerde que también el Sevilla. Hubo muchos clubes que se enfadaron porque mostrábamos imágenes que no eran de su agrado", afirmó. El periodista también reivindicó la forma de trabajar del equipo de El Golazo de GOL. "No digo desde la verdad, porque cada uno tiene su verdad, pero desde nuestra honestidad hicimos lo que pensábamos en cada momento que era lo más interesante", señaló. Lama recordó además la apuesta que supuso realizar un informativo deportivo de dos horas diarias, de 14.00 a 16.00 horas, incluso durante el verano. "Fuimos valientes", afirmó. El formato combinaba información, reportajes y tertulias y, según el periodista, contribuyó a elevar la competencia entre los programas deportivos de televisión. "Me da pena que desaparezcan los informativos", reconoció Lama, que considera que la existencia de varias propuestas deportivas obligaba a todos a luchar más y ofrecer un mejor producto. "El gran favorecido siempre era el espectador", concluyó.

articles.body:
AAA and WWE presented Worlds Collide in Chicago, with the event airing exclusively on YouTube on Wednesday.

CM Punk, Rey Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix, Roxanne Perez and Je'Von Evans were among the WWE Superstars who faced AAA's top talent at Allstate Arena.

What happened, how did each match grade out, and who emerged victorious? Find out in this recap.

CM Punk, Rey Mysterio, and El Grande Americano vs. Dominik Mysterio, JD McDonagh, and Omos

Penta and Rey Fenix vs. Los Perros del Mal (Daga and Berto)

AAA Reina de Reinas Championship: La Catalina (c) vs. Roxanne Perez

Six-Woman Tag Team match: Fatal Influence (Jacy Jayne, Lainey Reid, and Fallon Henley) vs. Las Toxicas (Flammer, La Hiedra, and Maravilla)

AAA Cruiserweight Championship No. 1 Contender's match: Axiom vs. Mini Vikingo vs. Je'Von Evans vs. EK Prosper

La Parka, Mr. Iguana, Mascarita Sagrada and Adelicious vs. Mini Abismo Negro, Brad Baylor, Ricky Smokes, and Myka Lockwood

Participants: La Parka, Mr. Iguana, Adelicious, and Mascarita Sagrada vs. The Vanity Project (Brad Baylor, Ricky Smokes, and Myka Lockwood) and Mini Abismo Negro

The lucha team of La Parka, Iguana, Adelicious, and Sagrada kicked off the show on a fan-pleasing note, picking up a hard-fought victory in an energy-filled tag match.

The heels did a fantastic job of drawing heat and cheating their way to the advantage, but late dives by Adelicious, Iguana, and La Parka wiped out The Vanity Project at ringside.

Sagrada outmaneuvered the larger Mini Abismo Negro and scored the win for his team from there.

Adelicious, La Parka, Mr. Iguana, and Mascarita Sagrade defeated The Vanity Project and Mini Abismo Negro

Early, the emphasis was on Lockwood and for the most part, she performed up to the moment. She struggled to keep pace with Adelicious at a point or two, but she did not let the stage adversely affect her.

It never ceases to amaze how much fun and energy these multi-competitor tag matches pack in them. This really had no rhyme or reason, and it did not reinvent the wheel, but it was an immensely good time and featured some solid spotlight for Lockwood.

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee defeated Big Cass (Raw, September 28); Jack Cartwheel lost to Rey Fenix (AAA TripleMania, September 13)

Two of the best, most athletic cruiserweights clashed in the night's second match, a battle of the Superstars who gravity forgot, dedicated by Corey Graves to the family of the late Ben "Pac/Adrian Neville" Satterley, with whom the play-by-play man teamed and feuded.

Non-stop action defined the night's second match, a showcase of two competitors with the speed, agility, athleticism, and never-say-die approach matched by few.

Late in the match, Lee delivered Diamond Dust, stunning Cartwheel. The underdog competitor fought through it and delivered a beautiful crucifix bomb and it looked like he might win.

Lee recovered, though, got his knees up at an opportune time, and finished with Operation Dragon for the win.

Lee is such an extraordinary athlete that it is rare for a main roster star to be able to keep up with him at full speed. It was nice to see him mix it up with someone like Cartwheel, who can not only keep up with the former tag team champion, but also test him.

Cartwheel showed it here. There are a lot of people who may not be familiar with his game but after this one, they should be. One of the most unique and creative in-ring performers in the sport.

articles.title: World Grand Prix: Gerwyn Price books all-Welsh quarter-final with Jonny Clayton as Nathan Aspinall breezes through
articles.summary: Nathan Aspinall and Ryan Joyce claimed straight-set wins to also reach the last eight in Leicester; Gerwyn Price beat Ross Smith 3-0 after Jonny Clayton despatched Wessel Nijman 3-1; watch the World Grand Prix throughout the week live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Price, among the tournament favourites after Luke Littler's shock early exit, followed his opening-round victory over Sebastian Białecki by dropping just four legs to despatch Smith at the Mattioli Arena.

The 2020 champion was outscored by Smith - having posted the highest average of the first round - but dropped just four legs during his 3-0 win, securing him a meeting with World Cup of Darts partner Clayton on Friday evening.

Clayton opened with three consecutive ton-plus checkouts and made four in total during a 3-1 victory over Wessel Nijman, where a 93.08 average and some remarkable finishing pushed him past the 12th seed.

Ryan Joyce breezed into the quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Danny Noppert, as Luke Woodhouse - who stunned Littler in the first round - was knocked out after losing 3-0 to Nathan Aspinall in a one-sided contest.

How Price and Clayton set up all-Welsh showdown

Price averaged 101.61 on Monday night but was over 10 points lower against Smith, where he recovered from being broken early with a 13-darter to match it in the next and then claim the opening set in a final-leg decider.

The world No 4 took out an 86 finish on his way to winning the second set and nailed an 80 checkout early in the third, where Smith took out 116 to break and extend the match before Price closed out victory on D18.

"I don't think it was a great game and I don't think we played brilliant," Price admitted to Sky Sports . "What we did do in patches was start well and finish well, but the bits in between were a little bit rubbish.

"I know he [Clayton] is chasing a Grand Slam spot, so the pressure is on him. I think he got lucky first round - hopefully he doesn't get lucky in the next round!"

Clayton won the opening set in straight legs after three consecutive ton-plus finishes, immediately breaking with a 112 checkout, taking out 116 to hold throw and then nailing a 125 finish on the bullseye.

Nijman responded to Clayton pinching a leg with a 90 finish to take the second set in a final-leg decider, before 'The Ferret' regained the lead by starting the third with another bullseye finish to take out 126.

Clayton, who posted eight maximums alongside his impressive finishing, then reeled off four of the next six legs to reach the quarter-finals for a third consecutive year.

"My scoring was good but, to be fair, Wessel [Nijman] missed a few chances on doubles and he gave me a few chances," Clayton told Sky Sports . "The two bullseyes were good, the 126 was good and I have a big smile."

Aspinall ends Woodhouse's Grand Prix run

Woodhouse halted Littler's title defence on Monday but saw his own hopes quickly ended by Aspinall, as he lost the first four legs before nailing a 135 finish to break throw.

Aspinall - who averaged 96.27 and crashed in eight 180s - immediately broke back and then took out 104 to open a two-set buffer, before reeling off three consecutive legs from 2-0 down in the next to confirm his quarter-final spot.

"As long as I can handle the pressure, which I think I have shown in these two games in the key moments, I am going to be tough to beat this week," Aspinall told Sky Sports . "If it all comes together, I am one of the best players in the world. Everybody knows that but I have to prove it."

Aspinall will next face Joyce, who dominated an opening match of the evening where Noppert won just three legs and seemed frustrated about the stage floorboards moving.

articles.title: Arizona State hockey coach placed on paid leave as investigation into tragic workout continues
articles.summary: Arizona State University placed hockey coach Greg Powers on paid leave as the investigation into a workout that left a player in a coma continues.
articles.body: Arizona State University has placed head coach of the men's hockey program Greg Powers on paid administrative leave as the school continues to investigate a workout that left a player in a coma. Sophomore and St. Louis Blues prospect Matthew Mayich has been in a coma since the August 20 workout the team held, run by an ex-Army Green Beret. On Wednesday, ASU athletic director Graham Rossini announced that Powers — who has led the program since it debuted at the D-1 level for the 2015-16 season — had been placed on leave the previous day. FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS "Our focus continues to be on Matthew and his family, and on our student-athletes to make sure they have the support they need during this time and as the season begins," Rossini said in a statement. "We have continued to collect as much information as possible. After thorough and careful deliberation, I believe this is the best move to provide stability for the hockey program." Assistant coach Mike Corbett will be behind the bench when the Sun Devils open their season on the road against Lindenwood University. An interim head coach will be named at a later date. Powers' leave comes just days after seven members of the Sun Devil hockey program released a letter through an attorney that disputed certain findings of the school's initial review into the incident. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The 26-page letter sent to ASU President Michael Crow noted that the entire coaching staff — which was present at the workout — was, to that point, still with the program. "The head coach and his assistant coaches were all on the field on August 20, all remain in their positions, and together they decide our playing time, scholarship levels, and roster status," the letter reads, per The Athletic. "No one has separated us from them since that morning. "We should not have to choose between telling the truth about August 20 and keeping what we have worked our whole lives for." Mayich remains in the hospital, with his family's attorney, Robert Carey, saying that he has "zero chance of recovery." He was selected by the Blues in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL Draft.

articles.title: What happened to Phil Mickelson? Golf star sought help for ‘family trauma and addiction’
articles.summary: Phil Mickelson recently checked himself into an addiction treatment centre while dealing with family trauma and personal issues, according to a report by
articles.body: Phil Mickelson recently checked himself into an addiction treatment centre while dealing with family trauma and personal issues, according to a report by TMZ Sports. A representative for the six-time major champion told TMZ Sports, “Phil was seeking treatment for family trauma and addiction.” Mickelson entered the facility voluntarily and has since left, the report said. The 56-year-old golfer has stayed away from most professional golf this year while dealing with a private family matter. His treatment comes months after his representatives said his main focus was his family. Mickelson has also spoken publicly about his past gambling addiction and the effect it had on his life.Phil Mickelson sought treatment after family health matterMickelson’s treatment follows a period in which he largely stepped away from professional golf. Earlier this year, his representatives said he needed time to deal with a private family health matter.In June, Mickelson’s representatives said, “Mr. Mickelson’s priority is to become the husband, father, and man his family deserves. Right now, that means giving his full attention to a private family health matter. He understands that parts of his life are public, but his family’s private matters are not.”Mickelson has played very little competitive golf in 2026. Golf Digest reported in June that he had announced an extended break from competition while dealing with a family health matter. The report also said he had played only once during the year at that point.The latest report does not give details about when Mickelson entered the treatment centre or how long he stayed there. It only says he sought treatment recently and has already left the facility. His representative described the reason as treatment for family trauma and addiction.Phil Mickelson has spoken about gambling addictionMickelson has previously been open about his problems with gambling. In 2023, he acknowledged that his gambling had gone beyond what he could control and said it had affected people close to him.He also said he had received professional help for years. His comments came after reports and claims about the scale of his gambling, including allegations made by former sports bettor Billy Walters. Mickelson has previously rejected some of those claims while acknowledging that gambling had been a serious issue in his life.His personal life also came under renewed attention this year after Golf Digest reported allegations involving a female employee at The Farms Golf Club in San Diego. The employee accused Mickelson of “nonconsensual and inappropriate physical contact.” Mickelson’s representative later confirmed that he had resigned from the club.Mickelson’s lawyer disputed the account and called the article a “drive-by shooting.” Golf Digest said it gave Mickelson’s legal team an opportunity to provide video that would contradict its reporting, but no such footage was provided.The treatment report does not connect the facility stay to those allegations. articles.title: Chloe Kim opens up about ADHD diagnosis: ‘I was struggling’ despite intense snowboarding focus
articles.summary: Chloe Kim has revealed that she was recently diagnosed with ADHD after years of struggling with brain fog, exhaustion and difficulty staying present in
articles.body: Chloe Kim has revealed that she was recently diagnosed with ADHD after years of struggling with brain fog, exhaustion and difficulty staying present in everyday life. The Olympic snowboarder said she had reached “a really bad place” before deciding to speak with a psychiatrist. That conversation helped her understand why some parts of life felt so difficult, even though she could focus intensely while snowboarding. Kim, who won silver at the 2026 Winter Olympics after two earlier halfpipe golds, said the diagnosis gave her a clearer explanation for what she had been experiencing.Chloe Kim explains why ADHD was hard to spot while snowboardingKim said she did not first think ADHD could explain her struggles because of the way she could focus on the slopes. “Actually, I recently found out I have ADHD.” she said in an Instagram video shared as part of her Qelbree partnership.“For years, I was struggling, but once I finally opened up to my doctor, it was like everything suddenly clicked,” Kim said.She also explained that snowboarding gave her a level of focus that felt very different from the rest of her life. Speaking on The School of Greatness, she said, “Because you’ve got to be in the flow on the slopes. You can’t be distracted in the air,” she said. “I was so focused whenever… I had my snowboard attached to my feet, like tunnel vision.”Away from snowboarding, Kim said she often felt exhausted. “After snowboarding, I didn’t want to go hang out with friends. Like, I didn’t want to go out. Like, I just wanted to rest,” she explained. Her routine, she said, became: “Snowboard, recover. Snowboard, recover.”Kim also spoke about her imagination and how it helped her approach new tricks. “I feel like I never really experienced fear,” she said. “I have a very vivid imagination. So I feel like if I wanted to try a trick, I could visualize it before, without even doing it.”Chloe Kim uses lists, reminders and Qelbree to manage ADHDAfter getting answers from a psychiatrist, Kim said she has been using simple routines to stay organised. “Well, I love lists and phone reminders, and having a consistent routine helps me so much,” she said.Kim has also said she takes Qelbree in the mornings. According to Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Qelbree is viloxazine extended-release, a once-daily, non-stimulant prescription medicine approved in the US for ADHD in adults and children aged six and older. Kim discussed the medication while partnering with the company.Her diagnosis has also changed how she looks at the difference between her life on the snow and her life away from it. The intense concentration that helped her compete at the highest level did not mean she could not have ADHD.For Kim, speaking to a psychiatrist finally helped connect experiences she had struggled to explain for years. articles.title: Cubs turn to veteran Kevin Gausman — whose shoulder feels ‘good enough’ — to start in must-win Game 2
articles.summary: SAN DIEGO — Six days ago, Kevin Gausman faced uncertainty surrounding whether he would be available to pitch for the Chicago Cubs in the National League wild...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO — Six days ago, Kevin Gausman faced uncertainty surrounding whether he would be available to pitch for the Chicago Cubs in the National League wild-card series.

The left shoulder injury Gausman sustained during his final regular-season start last week while making a diving tag at third base did not feel great the next day. The Cubs tried to give the 35-year-old ample time to recover before turning to Gausman for the Game 2 start Wednesday night, facing elimination against the San Diego Padres .

As for how his shoulder feels now, "we're going to find out," Gausman said Tuesday after the Cubs' ugly 8-0 Game 1 loss.

"It feels all right, good enough to go out there and give it everything I got," he said. "So that's what I'm going to do."

This certainly isn't an ideal setup with the Cubs going into a must-win game and Gausman not 100% healthy. But it's what they're working with at this point.

These moments are why the Cubs wanted to acquire the battle-tested veteran at the trade deadline. And given the circumstances, if his outing isn't trending well early, manager Craig Counsell has multiple options he can turn to in an all-hands-on-deck reality with the season on the line.

Those choices might include right-hander Clay Holmes , who pitched out of the bullpen the first seven years of his career until signing with the New York Mets as a starter before the 2025 season, or left-handers David Peterson and Shota Imanaga . High-leverage arms Daniel Palencia and Ryan Zeferjahn also are well-rested.

Gausman credited the Cubs training staff for even getting him in this position to pitch Wednesday. He admitted he didn't know if this would be possible a few days ago.

Although the injury is to his non-throwing shoulder, his left side is an important cog within his delivery, especially with his big 13-inch mitt. Gausman needs his left front side to be strong because of how he grips his glove as leverage to pull himself down to bring his right arm through.

"The weird thing is I've had shoulder injuries before, but it's always been the right one, so this one's been a little different," Gausman said. "Trying to feel out the movements and what I'm maybe going to have to change a little bit out there to be able to do what I want to do. … It's been a little crazy."

Gausman has plenty of recent experience pitching in big playoff games. He pitched into at least the sixth inning of all five of his 2025 postseason starts with the Toronto Blue Jays , posting a 3.03 ERA and striking out 26 and walking eight in 29 2/3 innings.

"Try to treat it as a normal game," Gausman said. "You really can't when they're waving towels out there. But try to just stay in the moment and trust yourself and trust the team behind you. Go out there and give it everything."

Gausman threw a pregame bullpen session Tuesday to test how he felt and believes his left shoulder held up well enough to allow him to make adjustments when he needed to.

"He's been great ever since I've been teammates with him, and just seeing the success he's had in the past — he's been in moments like this before," catcher Carson Kelly said Tuesday. "So we're going to rely on him and give it our all."

articles.title: 76ers news: Tyrese Maxey's hilarious response to LeBron leaving in helicopter

articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are less than three weeks away from kicking off their 2026-27 season, with new faces Jaylen Brown and LeBron James now in the fold. The 76ers have gotten training camp underway this week as they look to build some synergy before the new season kicks off.

James has been widely reported to be living in New York City while playing with the 76ers, and was recently spotted leaving the team's practice in a helicopter to head back to the Big Apple.

Now, 76ers star Tyrese Maxey has reacted to that development , referencing his own car issues earlier this week.

"One of us left in a helicopter, the other one was sitting on the curb," he said, per PHLY Sixers on X, formerly Twitter.

Regardless of where he spends his downtime, James figures to play a big role for the 76ers on the court this season, having already adjusted to playing a less burdensome offensive role last year for the Los Angeles Lakers , when he often took a backseat to both Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves in terms of handling the ball.

Still, questions persist about how the 76ers will divvy up the touches this year, with Maxey, James, Brown, and Joel Embiid all accustomed to getting their fair share of time with the basketball. Skeptics have also pointed out defensive concerns, shooting issues, as well as questions about health and availability as reasons to doubt the 76ers this year.

In any case, Philadelphia will look to start answering those questions when their regular season gets underway on October 20 on the road vs the defending champion New York Knicks .

articles.title: Tom Izzo on placing limitations on coach movement and buyouts: ‘That’s all fair’
articles.summary: Michigan State basketball head coach Tom Izzo doesn’t have a problem with limitations placed on coach movement and buyouts. Speaking to reporters on Wednesda...
articles.body:
Michigan State basketball head coach Tom Izzo doesn't have a problem with limitations placed on coach movement and buyouts. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Izzo said if administrators want to enforce that, then he will support the move.

"That's all fair," Izzo said, per Connor Earegood of Detroit News . "I still have a buyout. 32 years, I might be the only guy in captivity that has a buyout. I have no problem with that. These people out there that are shooting their mouths off that coaches can leave whenever they want; most coaches have pretty good buyouts. If you ask me, if that's what administrators wanted to enforce, I'm all for it. I have no problem with that.

"I do think what you own over 32 years or 40 years compared to people who haven't even played in a game in college, that's a ridiculous argument by a couple of key people that we all know who they are on VidCon TV, which is ridiculous."

This week, the Senate passed the Protect College Sports Act by a 77-22 vote. Izzo supports the bill that includes the "Lane Kiffin Rule," which would prevent any FBS coaches from leaving a new head coaching job in-season at a new school before the end of their team's season.

Before the passage of the Protect College Sports Act, senators considered a proposed amendment that would have put a $5 million salary cap on college football coaches. The amendment failed to be included.

Michigan State does not have to worry about Izzo's buyout because it's not like the school will fire him. In December, Izzo received a $1 million raise in his five-year contract that automatically renews annually. He makes around $7.2 million per year, according to ESPN.

"Coach Izzo is the ultimate Spartan — someone whose work ethic and devotion to our student-athletes, this university, and the broader MSU community are unmatched," Michigan State president Kevin M. Guskiewicz said at the time. "We believe deeply in his ability to uphold our values, develop champions, and continue building one of college basketball's premier programs."

Tom Izzo has been Michigan State's head coach since 1995. During his time with the Spartans, Izzo has won 11 Big Ten regular-season championships and six Big Ten tournament championships. He has reached the Final Four eight times and won the national title in 2000.

articles.title: Phillies news: Bryce Harper knew he had to 'come up big' with HR after error in 7th
articles.summary: Philadelphia Phillies superstar Bryce Harper said he knew he needed to deliver after a seventh-inning defensive misplay nearly helped end his team’s season W...
articles.body:
Philadelphia Phillies superstar Bryce Harper said he knew he needed to deliver after a seventh-inning defensive misplay nearly helped end his team's season Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves .

With Game 2 tied 1-1, Drake Baldwin's fly ball to right glanced off Harper's glove and was scored a double, allowing Sean Murphy to score the go-ahead run. Matt Olson 's sacrifice fly later made it 3-1. Phillies chief video editor Cam shared Harper's postgame interview with NBC Sports on X, formerly Twitter, after Philadelphia rallied for a 4-3, 10-inning win at Truist Park.

"Yeah, I got to come up big, right? Obviously, you know, ball in right field. Probably should have been caught, obviously. So I got to come through for my team right there"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The two-time NL MVP did exactly that one inning later. Kyle Schwarber opened the eighth with a 447-foot home run off Dylan Lee , and Harper followed with a 418-foot solo shot to tie the game 3-3.

The play in right was not officially scored as an error, but Harper treated it as a ball he should have caught. His homer gave him two RBIs after he drove in Trea Turner with a first-inning single.

Alec Bohm then completed the comeback in the 10th, sending a 357-foot opposite-field homer off Didier Fuentes for a 4-3 lead. Andrew Painter protected it with his third scoreless inning of relief in his postseason debut.

The victory evened the best-of-three Wild Card Series at 1-1 and forced a winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday with the Phillies' season still on the line . The winner will advance to face the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS beginning Saturday.

articles.title: OU football coach Brent Venables stands by John Mateer: 'John's our starting quarterback'
articles.summary: OU football coach Brent Venables says John Mateer remains the starting quarterback ahead of the Red River Rivalry against Texas.
articles.body:
NORMAN — OU football coach Brent Venables is standing by quarterback John Mateer for now.

After Venables said backups Whitt Newbauer and Bowe Bentley took "a lot" of reps during Wednesday's practice, he was asked if either of them will play against Texas in the Red River Rivalry next weekend.

"I have no idea," Venables said. "We're not there right now. John's our starting quarterback."

Venables said he has liked how Mateer has responded during the bye week after turning the ball over three times in the first half of the Sooners' road loss to Georgia last weekend, a game in which the coaches weighed benching Mateer.

With Mateer seemingly moving on as OU's starter, the coaching staff will need to look for ways to build back up his confidence, which Venables admitted last Saturday isn't "sky high" at the moment.

"How he responds — all of those things have been really good," Venables said. "Probably a lot better than you or I, or any of us could ever to be honest."

Oklahoma Sooners vs Georgia Bulldogs in Week 4 college football, see top photos

As for Newbauer and Bentley — listed as "ORs" on the depth chart — Venables is pleased with the progress he's seen them make. Mateer and Newbauer have mostly split the majority of the snaps this season with Bentley getting around 20% of them daily, Venables said.

Venables said each has their strength and weaknesses but pointed to their lack of experience in games.

Furthermore, Venables shared his thoughts on why most schools lack established backup quarterback in this day and age in college football.

"The money, the opportunity to go somewhere and play to make money," Venables said. "And then a school willing to to pay for two really expensive quarterbacks is another layer to it. But somebody willing to go somewhere and maybe not be the guy, guaranteed, right away. It's a little harder than you want it to be."

Bye weeks are a time for reflection and reevaluation. The Sooners' coaches have undergone extensive reevaluations of every aspect of the program this week during a disappointing season thus far.

For now, Venables is hitching his wagon to Mateer. That could always change but he's liked the response from the entire offensive unit this week as they prepare to face the Longhorns next weekend.

"We want to be a more consistent unit, obviously," Venables said. "That side of the ball has had to work a little harder, and sometimes it feels like we're going upstream. Things have been a little choppier than you want them to be. Good play, negative play. First down, have a delay. First down, tackle for loss. We want to be able to play in a better rhythm that comes from a lot of different things.

"It's a lot of little things. ... We've got to do a better job overall of executing more consistently."

articles.title: Mike Macdonald on Rashid Shaheed's limited production: "The ball will find him"
articles.summary: In June, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he was "excited to see" what receiver Rashid Shaheed would do in the offense, given the benefit of having the ful...
articles.body:
In June, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he was " excited to see " what receiver Rashid Shaheed would do in the offense, given the benefit of having the full offseason and training camp to prepare for his first full year with the team.

Through three games, Shaheed's offensive production has been limited to six catches for 53 yards.

On Wednesday, Macdonald was asked about Shaheed's numbers.

"I don't know what exactly his numbers are," Macdonald said. "I know the ball's finding [ Jaxon Smith-Njigba ] a lot right now. Sheed's doing a great job. Because of the question, I'm assuming you're thinking the ball's not finding him as much, but it will. I think we've just got to stick to our process. There's always something that maybe we want to improve in our game, but we've just got to keep attacking it, stick with it, make some tweaks in how we approach everything and trust that the ball goes in the right direction and it'll find him, but he's doing a good job."

In contrast, Smith-Njigba has 27 catches for 405 yards and six touchdowns. And Cooper Kupp has eight catches for 101 yards and a touchdown.

Shaheed also contributes on special teams, with seven punt returns for 67 yards and seven kickoff returns for 190. Still, the full contribution seems to be falling short of the $17 million per year in compensation that Shaheed is receiving.
